clue.text: What you'd give to avoid awful beer in some measure

indicators.note: the shuffled beer sits in the middle of the measurement word

parts.note: width is a measurement, one dimension of a thing

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the letters of beer are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone sizing up an unpleasant pint they would rather steer clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' gives EBER, which 'in' sets inside the measurement. 'measure' looks like a unit of drink; it is a dimension.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving something or someone a wide berth is the idiom for keeping well away to avoid them.

clue.text: Whether to start chopping up bad tree? Sleep on it

indicators.note: to start asks for only the opening letter of the word whether
chopping up a tree breaks it into pieces, so the letters of bad tree are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone debating whether to fell a diseased tree and deciding to sleep on the decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopping up' rearranges BADTREE into ATERBED, after W. 'Sleep on it' looks like the advice to wait a night; it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterbed is a bed, a mattress filled with water, which is what you sleep on.

clue.text: Drink laced with drug leads to dozy state

indicators.note: a drink laced with something has it slipped inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A spiked drink leaves someone groggy and half asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a drowsy, half-awake reverie, the state of being dozy and far away.

clue.text: Top dog taken up river after a dance

indicators.note: after places the turned-round river behind the a in the answer

parts.note: the top dog in an organisation is the boss

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means read from the bottom upwards, so the river is reversed

parts.note: the Avon is an English river, the one at Stratford

explanation.surface: A leading dog carried upstream after joining a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' gives NOVA, which 'after' sets behind the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian dance and musical style related to samba.

clue.text: Object, clad in torn clothing

indicators.note: one word is dressed in the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: rent is an old word for torn, as in clothes rent apart
an aim is an object or goal

explanation.surface: An item dressed in ragged garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old-fashioned literary word for clothing or garments.

clue.text: House, scene, of drama for security prisoner?

parts.note: the stage is where drama is played out

explanation.surface: A house serves as the setting for a play about someone held for security.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'scene' is a stray mark; the printed clue reads 'scene of drama'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held as security that demands will be met, hence a prisoner taken as security.

clue.text: Put back into exercise?

parts.note: the idiom of putting one's back into a task is taken literally: an exercise where you lie back and then raise the body using the back and stomach

explanation.surface: Advice to make more effort in a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-up is a gym exercise in which you rise from lying on your back, so the back is truly put into it.

clue.text: Use pass

definitions.meaning: to use up money or energy is to expend it
to pass time is to while it away, as in a pleasant afternoon

explanation.definitionFit: Spending is both using up resources and passing time, as in spending a week away.

clue.text: Retaliation, when, given the bird because of rubbish

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
for can mean because of, as in jumping for joy
tat is cheap worthless rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone who gets the bird for poor work hits back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given the bird' usually means booed; here it simply supplies a bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat is an idiom for retaliation in kind, one blow for another.

clue.text: Take off, having put earnings across the bar

indicators.note: the pay is placed across the bar, enclosing it

parts.note: pay is what one earns
a rod is a bar of metal or wood

explanation.surface: A drinker leaves after putting wages over the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like departing; it is the noun-like verb for mimicking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off someone is to mimic them for comic effect, which is to parody them.

clue.text: Lock casual worker away from femme, fatale

indicators.note: the casual worker is taken away from the femme fatale, removing those letters

parts.note: a temptress is a seductive woman, a femme fatale (the comma is a stray mark in the print)
a temp is a temporary or casual office worker

explanation.surface: An office temp gets clear of a dangerous seductress.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair.

clue.text: Copper isn't giving up first of promotions, struggling to leading rank

annotationWithheld.why: Copper isn't giving up first of promotions, struggling to leading rank (9): no parse found; ISN'T, P (first of promotions), TO and R give only I,S,N,T,P,T,O,R, not INSPECTOR, and no reading of 'giving up' or 'leading rank' supplies E and C
annotationWithheld.clue: Copper isn't giving up first of promotions, struggling to leading rank

clue.text: Unfurl map in temper and go berserk

indicators.note: the unrolled map goes inside the word for temper

parts.note: rage is a fit of temper

indicators.note: unfurling a map spreads it out of its folds, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper trying to open a map, and going wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfurl' gives MPA, which 'in' sets inside the word for temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about violently, which is going berserk.

clue.text: Add iron alloy 'to make automaton

indicators.note: an alloy is a melting together of metals, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Instructions for building a robot by blending iron into a metal mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alloy' is the mixing signal; the apostrophe before 'to' is a print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a robot made to look human, a kind of automaton.

clue.text: Really go out of one's way here, eh?

definitions.text: Really go out of one's way here, eh?

parts.words: Really go out of one's way here, eh?
parts.note: going out of one's way normally means taking great trouble; read literally, the furthest place one could travel to, as in the idiom about going anywhere for someone

explanation.surface: A comment on someone taking enormous trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The most remote places on the globe; going there is the idiom for making every effort.

clue.text: Right-winger at first cried off writing book

indicators.note: at first says the shuffled word comes first, before the right-winger
off means wrong or spoiled, so the letters of cried are rearranged

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, on the political right

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician withdrew at the outset from writing a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' gives DIREC and 'at first' puts it before the politician. 'cried off' looks like the phrase for withdrawing; 'writing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A directory is a reference book listing names and addresses, such as a telephone book.

clue.text: A labour union least missing leader of militant element

parts.note: L is a common abbreviation for Labour

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: the least possible amount is the minimum

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A trade union, short of its militant leader, at its weakest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' and 'leader of' remove one M from MINIMUM, leaving MINIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Aluminium (aluminum in American spelling) is a metallic chemical element.

clue.text: First off, lad traps park keeper in greenhouse, maybe

indicators.note: one piece catches and holds the other inside it
the opening letter is taken off

parts.note: a boy is a lad
a ranger looks after a park or forest

explanation.surface: A boy shuts a park warden inside a glasshouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First off' cuts BOY to OY, which 'traps' RANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glasshouse for growing orange trees, a type of greenhouse, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Living on sandwiches?

parts.note: living is read as a livelihood, the basic source of income, while the surface suggests a diet of sandwiches, which are made of the same ingredients

explanation.surface: Someone surviving on a diet of sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread and butter is the idiom for one's basic livelihood or main source of income.

clue.text: Show support for military installation

parts.note: to air an opinion is to show it publicly
a base is what supports something

explanation.surface: Displaying backing for an army camp.
explanation.definitionFit: An air base is a military airfield, a type of military installation.

clue.text: Stray American soldier turning up in uniform

indicators.note: the soldier is placed inside the uniform

parts.note: dress means uniform, as in full dress

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: GI is the usual name for an American soldier

explanation.surface: A wandering American serviceman appears in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' gives IG, which 'in' sets inside the uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to stray from the main subject.

clue.text: Entertain wreck exploration right at the bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the end, so this piece goes last

parts.note: a dive explores a sunken wreck

explanation.surface: Amusing diving around a shipwreck with the right gear on the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert someone is to amuse or entertain them.

clue.text: Ivory perhaps incorporated is gold as well?

parts.note: INC is the abbreviation for incorporated, as in company names
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Asking whether an ivory company is golden too.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivories are teeth in slang, and an incisor is a front cutting tooth.

clue.text: Separate riddle

definitions.meaning: to separate coarse from fine material by straining it
a riddle is a coarse ..., and to riddle is to sift

explanation.definitionFit: A sieve both separates and is called a riddle, a gardener's word for a coarse sifting screen.

clue.text: Be a shining example — .good to hear

parts.note: to listen is to hear attentively

explanation.surface: Praise for someone being a model who is pleasant to listen to.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to shine and sparkle with reflected light.

clue.text: Coaches, or something along those lines?

definitions.meaning: railway carriages, joined together to make up one
something that runs along railway lines

explanation.definitionFit: A train is made of coaches and travels on railway lines; the plural definition names its parts.

clue.text: Justify one extra being scrambled before end of game

indicators.note: scrambled letters are mixed up, so one extra is rearranged
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An extra player being drafted in at the end of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being scrambled' rearranges ONEEXTRA into EXONERAT, and 'end of' adds E from game.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear of blame, to vindicate or justify.

clue.text: Picture one apparently wise individual …

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a mage is a magician or wise man, one who appears learned

explanation.surface: A portrait of someone who seems wise.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness.

clue.text: … while talking to a plant

indicators.note: talking points to a word spoken rather than written

parts.note: a while is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone chatting to a houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic herb, a garden plant.

clue.text: Proceeds very quickly from scam

parts.note: proceeds is read as income, not as moves on: cash made fast and without effort, such as a con brings

explanation.surface: Someone rushing away from a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy money is income gained without effort, often dishonestly.
